Associated Keywords: what is agentic seo, ai seo agent, agentic seo workflow, ai agent for seo audit
Friction: Every definition on this SERP describes what an agent does — it plans, it executes, it watches after publish, it acts at the autonomy you set. None of them describe what the agent does when it cannot see something. That is the failure mode that costs money: a system that could not verify a condition and reported a pass anyway, at a volume no human reviewed.
Logic: Define the category honestly first (multi-step tool-calling work rather than a report-and-wait tool), then argue that the buying test is not the capability list but the refusal list. Our own SEO agent publishes one — it states that 24 of its 81 catalogue checks are decided by evidence the crawl collects, that a limitation never becomes a pass, that the report does not claim GSC, traffic, or ranking data, and that it does not edit, deploy, or prove traffic impact. That disclosure is the thing to demand from any vendor. Trade-off worth naming: a refusal list makes a product look smaller, which is why most of the category does not publish one — and why our agent covers far less ground than the platforms it sits beside.
content_angle: The category's definitions are unanimous and all describe capability. This one defines the term the same way everyone else does — the query deserves a straight answer — and then supplies the test nobody supplies: what does it do when it cannot see? Quotes our own agent's published limits verbatim as the worked example, including the number of checks that are NOT evidence-backed. Names our own gap plainly: it does not generate, publish, edit, or deploy anything, which makes it a much narrower product than the platforms in this SERP. Anchors the volume risk in Google's scaled content abuse policy rather than in speculation.
